Bug_Title: Nullable injected fields and parameters should provide a default value
Bug_Details:
The @Value annotation does not guarantee that the property is defined. Particularly if a field or parameter is annotated as nullable,
it indicates that the developer assumes that the property may be undefined.
An undefined property may lead to runtime exceptions when the Spring framework tries to inject the autowired dependency during bean creation.
This rule raises an issue when a nullable field or parameter is annotated with @Value and no default value is provided.
Bug_Explanation: The 'undefinedProperty' field can be null if a value is not provided. This can lead to a NullPointerException when the field is used in the 'init' method. This issue is intentionally not fixed.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case 'testShowBug' calls the'showBug' method which returns the 'undefinedProperty' field. If the 'undefinedProperty' field is not initialized (which can happen if a value is not provided), the'showBug' method will return null. This triggers an assertion failure in the test case, as the 'assertNotNull' method expects a non-null value.
